content_text_body:
To increase your ability to engage in inclusive conversations, your first step is to assess your readiness and your team readiness to participate in this type of conversation.

### Build a safe work environment 
Conversations related to race, politics, sexual orientation, and religion can become challenging to handle in the workplace and can lead to polarization among your team. Nonetheless, creating a safe work environment where employees feel confident to express their opinions is the first step. Employees who trust their team and feel safe to express themselves will be more inclined to engage in meaningful dialogue without fear of being judged. Read these recommendations on [how to create a safe work environment for your employees](https://www.inc.com/peter-economy/5-ways-to-make-it-safe-for-employees-to-speak-up.html). 

### Model vulnerability
Share information about yourself including new learning regarding other cultures, philosophies, groups, etc. This action supports the idea that learning is encouraged to clarify assumptions, inform judgments, and promote deeper understanding through knowledge. 

### Listen, accept, and grow
Take time to listen to your employee's opinions, recognize and accept their emotions and values, and practice empathy. Leading the way for inclusive conversations is a process and each opportunity to practice meaningful dialogue allows you to continue growing. Increasing your knowledge about your own perspectives and the perspectives of others will help you to understand diverging viewpoints. 

Read this [article](https://www.forbes.com/sites/janicegassam/2019/11/27/the-pink-elephant-in-the-workplace-how-to-have-conversations-about-race-politics-and-religion-at-work/#4a224c156e2c) to learn more about difficult conversations in the workplace.
